summary: Online research for rev0109: preserve the execution focus by treating selector entry as an attestation/handoff step with digest-bound subjects and explicit tool hashes. HF and PyTorch docs reinforce why backend/cache/timing semantics remain unstable enough to bind in evidence, while SLSA/in-toto style subject digests motivated the new selector-entry receipt.

sources.title: Hugging Face attention backends
sources.relevance: attn_implementation is an explicit model-loading/runtime variable; trace receipts should not let backend identity drift.

sources.title: Hugging Face cache strategies
sources.relevance: Transformers exposes dynamic/static/offloaded/quantized cache options; cache identity must stay bound in the trace evidence.

sources.title: PyTorch CUDA Event docs
sources.relevance: CUDA events are synchronization markers for timing; timing receipts must distinguish diagnostic capture timing from named-hardware promotion timing.

sources.title: SLSA provenance v1.0
sources.relevance: Provenance binds produced artifacts through subject digests; rev0109 applies this to selector-entry handoff.

sources.title: in-toto attestation statement spec
sources.relevance: Attestation statements bind predicates to subjects; selector-entry is now represented as a separate predicate over the evaluation receipt, files, and tools.

sources.title: in-toto link predicate / ResourceDescriptor
sources.relevance: Resource descriptors with names and digests informed the semantic subject-name + sha256 structure.

risk_closed: receipt evidence_subject_set_sha256 could previously be asserted without recomputation in the selector gate
current evaluator/verifier tool hashes in a receipt were not compared to the actual tools used at selector entry
selector-entry itself did not emit a separate receipt binding the input receipt, actual files, and selector gate code
remaining_blockers: real public TinyLlama trace NPZ/provenance pair still absent in this capsule
selector-entry receipt is a handoff/control artifact, not named hardware timing
named hardware sparse-vs-dense timing remains required for promotion
